lines: Three-year history of recurrent sinus infections with two episodes of pneumonia in the last year, persistent cough, fatigue, and 10-pound weight loss

She reports a persistent cough, fatigue, and a recent unexplained weight loss of 10 pounds.

Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks monthly), denies abuse.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of fatigue, joint pain, and intermittent swelling of hands with episodes of fingers turning white and blue in cold temperatures

lines: Six-month history of fatigue, joint pain, and intermittent swelling of hands with episodes of fingers turning white and blue in cold temperatures
The patient returns to Rheumatology clinic for follow-up of her mixed connective tissue disease in the context of common variable immunodeficiency established one year prior.
She reports experiencing episodes of fingers turning white and blue when exposed to cold temperatures.
She also mentions difficulty swallowing and a recent onset of muscle weakness.
Her past medical history is significant for Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
- Chest tube thoracostomy (prior pneumonitis with parapneumonic effusion)
- Insulin glargine 24 units SC at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale SC before meals
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks monthly), denies abuse.
On physical examination, you note symmetrical swelling of the fingers and hands, and palpation of the muscles elicits tenderness.
Nailfold capillaroscopy shows dilated capillary loops.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive fatigue, joint pain, and occasional right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort

lines: Six-month history of progressive fatigue, joint pain, and occasional right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort

This 37-year-old woman with common variable immunodeficiency and mixed connective tissue disease presents with a 6-month history of fatigue, joint pain, and occasional right upper quadrant discomfort.
Her past medical history is significant for Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
- Chest tube thoracostomy (prior pneumonitis with parapneumonic effusion)
- Insulin glargine 24 units SC at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale SC before meals
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
She denies any history of alcohol abuse, drug use, or high-risk sexual behaviors.
On physical examination, she has mild hepatomegaly without splenomegaly.
Her skin and sclerae are anicteric.
Serologic testing shows positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and anti-smooth muscle antibodies (ASMA).

encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive fatigue, generalized weakness, 10-pound weight loss, orthostatic dizziness, and syncopal episodes

lines: Six-month history of progressive fatigue, generalized weakness, 10-pound weight loss, orthostatic dizziness, and syncopal episodes

The patient is a 39-year-old female with common variable immunodeficiency diagnosed in 2020, mixed connective tissue disease diagnosed in 2021, and autoimmune hepatitis diagnosed in 2022, who presents with a six-month history of progressive fatigue, generalized weakness, and a 10-pound weight loss.
She reports occasional episodes of dizziness, especially upon standing, and has had several episodes of syncope, along with persistent nausea and decreased appetite.
Her past medical history is significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus and autoimmune thyroiditis.
- Chest tube thoracostomy (prior pneumonitis with parapneumonic effusion)
- Insulin glargine 24 units SC at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale SC before meals
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks monthly), denies abuse.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, and her heart rate is 55 bpm.
She appears thin and has hyperpigmented creases on her palms.

encounters.cc: Persistent difficulty lifting right arm overhead and reaching high shelves several weeks after hospitalization for severe lung infection

lines: Persistent difficulty lifting right arm overhead and reaching high shelves several weeks after hospitalization for severe lung infection

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with common variable immunodeficiency and a history of mixed connective tissue disease and autoimmune hepatitis who presents for evaluation of persistent right upper extremity symptoms following recent hospitalization for a severe lung infection complicated by pleural fluid accumulation.
She reports persistent difficulty lifting her right arm overhead several weeks after hospitalization.
She describes trouble reaching high shelves and brushing her hair.
Her prior admission involved chest drainage due to accumulation of infected fluid in the right pleural cavity.
Recovery was complicated by discomfort near the upper chest wall, though the infection has resolved.
- Chest tube thoracostomy (prior pneumonitis with parapneumonic effusion)
- Insulin glargine 24 units SC at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale SC before meals
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO qAM, 10 mg PO qPM
Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks monthly), denies abuse.
On examination, motor strength and reflexes in the arm and forearm are preserved.
Passive and active range of motion at the glenohumeral joint is mostly intact.
When asked to push against the wall with both palms forward and arms extended, there is noticeable protrusion along the inner border of her right scapula.
No sensory deficits are detected over the shoulder or arm.
There is no muscle wasting or deformity over the deltoid, supraspinatus, or trapezius regions.
A plain radiograph of the shoulder shows no fractures or dislocations.
